title: Patrick Campbell on SaaS Pricing, Monetization, and Value Metrics
content:
Lenny Rachitsky: Welcome back to Lenny's Podcast. My guest today is Patrick Campbell, founder and former CEO of ProfitWell, acquired by Paddle. Patrick is one of the world's leading experts on SaaS pricing and retention.

Patrick Campbell: Thanks Lenny. Happy to talk pricing and revenue optimization.

Lenny Rachitsky: Why do so many SaaS startups struggle with pricing?

Patrick Campbell: Most founders treat pricing as a one-time decision rather than an ongoing process. They spend hundreds of hours building features and ten minutes deciding what to charge. The biggest mistake is pricing based on seat count instead of value metrics. Seat-based pricing penalizes account growth because customers try to minimize user licenses. Value metric pricing scales directly with customer utility—such as monthly active contacts, bandwidth consumed, or revenue generated.

Lenny Rachitsky: How often should a B2B company update or test its pricing?

Patrick Campbell: High-growth companies review pricing every six months and make meaningful pricing or packaging changes at least once a year. If you haven't touched your pricing in over twelve months, you are almost certainly underpricing by 30% to 50%. Monetization is 4x more powerful than acquisition for driving bottom-line growth.

Lenny Rachitsky: What is your advice on managing customer churn?

Patrick Campbell: Delinquent or credit card failure churn accounts for 20% to 40% of all SaaS churn. Before fixing voluntary churn, fix involuntary churn using automated dunning emails, in-app card updates, and smart retries.
